messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: dedicated-resv-pool us-east-1 at 95% GPU utilization; queue growth detected for enterprise tenant CobaltHealth. thread=3721009876

mia: paging oncall — reserved pool is effectively full. autoscaler keeps returning 429s from cloud API; new allocations stalled. CobaltHealth requests are piling up in the reservation queue.

anil: on it. joining. any immediate customer reports?

cust-success-bob: CobaltHealth reports spikes in completion latency and occasional 502s from our gateway starting ~00:18 UTC. They're seeing request timeouts at their app layer. I've told them we're investigating and will update.

leo: quick check — metrics: resv-pool gpu_util: 97% (5/5 gpus pinned by reservations), pending_queue: 420 -> trending up, autoscaler pending_ops=3 but cloud API returning 429 for scale requests. suspect autoscaler rate-limited by provider or token throttling.

samira: can we temporarily cap non-enterprise traffic to this pool? prefer to avoid customer impact for CobaltHealth. proposal: throttle best-effort tenants to 10% of baseline and evict long-running non-reserved sessions >30m.

ops-jen: I can run evict. command I'm about to run:```
resvctl evict --pool reserved-us-east-1 --selector tenant_type=best-effort --age-gt 30m --max-evict 25
```

ops-jen: running now...

ops-jen: evict returned: 18 sessions terminated, freed ~1.9 GPU-equivalents. pool utilization down to 92% but queue still high (380).

anil: good start. still need autoscaler flow fixed. leo can you dump autoscaler logs?

leo: past 15m autoscaler log snippet:```
ERROR 2026-03-15T00:22:11Z autoscaler.go:142 requestScale: cloudapi.ScaleProvision failed: status 429 RateLimitExceeded: quota exceeded for project
--- stack ---
github.com/redwood/autoscaler/scale
  /workspace/autoscaler/scale/request.go:74
```

leo: also seeing repeated token refresh errors immediately before 429s:```
WARN tokenmgr: refresh failed: 401 Unauthorized: invalid_client
```

eng-infra-oncall: tagging in. 401+429 pattern suggests stale credentials or abrupt policy change on provider side. Did we rotate any infra creds recently?

mia: not that I know of. I saw a creds rotation job run earlier in staging but not prod.

anil: immediate mitigations: 1) throttle non-enterprise traffic off reserved pool (samira/ops-jen in progress). 2) failover routing: send new CobaltHealth requests to a lower-memory variant (model-v-lite) if compatible. 3) provision ephemeral GPUs manually as a short-term hit.

leo: I can flip routing for CobaltHealth by adding a route override:```
redwoodctl routing set --tenant CobaltHealth --pool reserved-us-east-1 --fallback-model model-v-lite
```

samira: doing the override now.

samira: routing change applied. new requests should hit model-v-lite fallback (might increase token cost but reduces memory pressure).

ops-jen: provisioning 4 ephemeral pinned gpus in us-east-1 now (manual allocation) to handle reserve overflow. command:```
cloudctl provision --region us-east-1 --gpus 4 --type p-infer-temp --labels temp-incident-3721009876
```

deploy-bot: manual-provision job started id=provision-3721009876-1
deploy-bot: provision-3721009876-1 succeeded: 4 GPUs attached to pool reserved-us-east-1-temp at 00:31 UTC

ops-jen: after provisioning, pool util dropped to 78% and pending queue fell from 380 -> 60 in 8 minutes. latency for CobaltHealth now within 99th p99 ~2.1s (was 9-12s).

cust-success-bob: CobaltHealth on the line — reporting requests returning normally, some retries resolved. They want ETA for autoscaler fix.

leo: chasing autoscaler token path. short repro: tokenmgr attempted refresh and got 401 due to client_id mismatch (we had a codepath that falls back to legacy creds for a subset of requests). patch ready to push that forces the new token flow.

anil: ok patch + restart autoscaler. Who can restart safely?

leo: I will cut a hotfix and restart autoscaler in canary first (1 of 3 nodes). plan: deploy hotfix, watch scale attempts, then full roll.

leo: hotfix deployed to canary at 00:38 UTC. autoscaler started sending scale requests and got 202 accepted.

incident-bot: autoscaler: scale request accepted id=scale-372100-x1 status=accepted

leo: after hotfix, no more 401s in tokenmgr logs. cloudapi accepted scale ops. autoscaler resumed provisioning flow, queued ops processed.

ops-jen: scaling activity added 2 more GPUs automatically; pool now stable at 70% utilization. pending queue ~12.

mia: great. summary so far: root cause appears to be an autoscaler token refresh regression that caused provider 401/429s, blocking scale operations. That combined with a noisy set of best-effort sessions caused reserved pool exhaustion and customer-visible latency.

anil: action items to close in P1->postmortem: 1) permanent fix for token refresh codepath (owner: leo) 2) add rate-limit and retry-safe metrics/alerting on scale failures (owner: eng-infra-oncall) 3) flow to automatically throttle best-effort traffic when reserved pool exceeds threshold (owner: samira) 4) run tabletop for reserved-pool surge playbook with CS (owner: mia + cust-success-bob).

cust-success-bob: I'll schedule a 1:1 with CobaltHealth to go over what happened and the mitigations we did. they requested a 1-week follow-up demo showing SLA commitments.

eng-infra-oncall: I'll add an alert to catch repeated 401/429 sequences on autoscaler and trigger infra pager earlier.

leo: I'll push a follow-up PR to tighten token refresh tests and ship it by EOD.

samira: will draft a runbook step to evict long-running best-effort sessions under surge and wire it to the incident runbook.

mia: handing to postmortem. moving thread to #postmortems after quick notes. Thanks for fast work everyone. :white_check_mark:

anil: leaving post-incident notes in ops/incident-3721009876. we'll track RCA and timeline there. closing this active thread.

incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED by anil at 00:50 UTC. uptime impact window 00:18-00:38 UTC.
